Section(s): 2. Modeling; 2.1. Standard blocking model; 2.2. Complete and intermediate blocking models; 2.3. Cake filtration model

Text and equations in reading order:
    The flow rate Q can be calculated as a function of resistance R and membrane frontal area A using Darcy's law
(1) Q=\frac{P A}{R\mu}    [code: algebraic, computes Q, code proposes constitutive]
    where P is the trans-membrane pressure and $ \mu $ is the solution viscosity.
    In the standard model, membranes have straight cylindrical pores that decline in radius as solid matter accumulates on the pore walls [1,2]. The resistance can be calculated as a function of volume processed using Eq. (2), or time using Eq. (3)
(2) R=R_{0}\Bigg(1-\frac{K_{s}V}{2}\Bigg)^{-2}    [code: algebraic, computes R, code proposes constitutive]
    When a membrane fouls by the complete or intermediate blocking mechanism a portion of the pores are unavailable for flow. The available membrane area declines with permeate volume in the complete model according to Eq. (5), and in the intermediate model according to Eq. (6) $ ^{[2]} $
(5) \frac{A}{A_{0}}=1-\frac{K_{\mathrm{b}}}{J_{0}}V    [code: algebraic, computes A, code proposes constitutive]
(6) \frac{A}{A_{0}}=\exp(-K_{i}V)    [code: algebraic, computes A, code proposes constitutive]
    The constant $ K_{b} $ has units of $ s^{-1} $, and $ K_{i} $ has units of $ m^{-1} $. The equations are valid for both constant pressure and constant flow operation.
    In the cake filtration model the resistance to flow is increased by the presence of a cake layer on the membrane surface. The total resistance R will be the sum of the membrane resistance and the cake resistance. This can be calculated as a function of volume by Eq. (11) and time by Eq. (12)
(11) \frac{R}{R_{0}}=(1+K_{\mathrm{c}}J_{0}V)    [code: algebraic, computes R, code proposes constitutive]
(12) \frac{R}{R_{0}}=(1+2K_{\mathrm{c}}J_{0}^{2}t)^{1/2}    [code: algebraic, computes R, code proposes constitutive]
    where $ K_{c} $ has units of s/m $ ^{2} $. Eq. (13) describes volume as a function of time

Symbols:
  Q: flow rate [m^3/s] (computed)
  P: trans-membrane pressure [Pa] (computed)
  A: available membrane frontal area [m^2] (computed)
  R: resistance to filtration [m^{-1}] (computed)
  \mu: solution viscosity [kg/ms] (parameter)
  R_{0}: initial resistance to filtration [m^{-1}] (parameter)
  K_{s}: standard blocking constant [m^{-1}] (parameter)
  V: permeate volume processed per membrane area [m] (computed)
  K_{b}: complete blocking constant [s^{-1}] (parameter)
  J_{0}: initial flux [m/s] (variable)
  A_{0}: initial membrane frontal area [m^{2}] (parameter)
  K_{i}: intermediate blocking constant [m^{-1}] (parameter)
  K_{c}: cake filtration constant [s/m^{2}] (parameter)
  t: time [s] (variable)

Model-wide assumptions (already recorded, do not repeat):
  - Cake formation and complete pore blockage occur simultaneously.
  - Deposited aggregates are permeable.
  - Intermediate blocking assumes that a portion of the particles seal off pores and the rest accumulate on top of other deposited particles.
  - Standard blocking assumes that particles accumulate inside membranes on the walls of straight cylindrical pores.
  - Complete blocking assumes that particles seal off pore entrances and prevent flow.

Laws: 1, 2, 5, 6, 11, 12
